title: Given a number N, generate all structurally unique binary search trees that store values 1 through N. Explain how choosing each value as the root and recursively building left and right subtrees enumerates every shape.
shortTitle: Structurally Unique Binary Search Trees (Generate All Shapes)
keyPoints: For each value in [start, end], make it the root; smaller values form the left subtree, larger values form the right
Recursively generate all left-subtree shapes and all right-subtree shapes, then pair them under the chosen root
Empty range returns a list with one null, which represents a missing subtree and is essential for pairing
The number of distinct BST shapes for N values is the Nth Catalan number
Memoization by range avoids recomputation when counting, though generation rebuilds node objects
Practical only for small N because Catalan numbers grow exponentially

s1_definition.oneliner: Make each value the root, recurse to build all left and all right subtree shapes, and pair them under the root.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Structurally Unique BSTs** – generate every distinct binary search tree that stores values 1 through N.
- **Divide and conquer** – for each value as root, smaller values form the left subtree, larger values the right subtree.
- **Recursive pairing** – generate all left shapes and all right shapes, then create a tree for each (left, right) combination under the chosen root.
- **Empty-range sentinel** – returning a list with one null for an empty range lets pairing loops run correctly when a subtree is absent.
- **Catalan number** – the count of unique BST shapes for N values is C(N) = (2N)! / ((N+1)! * N!), which grows exponentially.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, an interest-tier lookup can be organized as a search tree over tier numbers 1 to N. Different tree shapes give different lookup depths. Analytics wants every valid shape to benchmark performance. Rajesh picks each tier as root, builds all shapes for the lower tiers on the left and higher tiers on the right, and combines them.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Generating unique BSTs for N=3:

  Choose root = 1:
    left = []         right = [2,3]
    left shapes: [null]   right shapes: 2 trees
    Trees:         1          1
                    \          \
                     2          3
                      \        /
                       3      2

  Choose root = 2:
    left = [1]        right = [3]
    left shapes: 1 tree   right shapes: 1 tree
    Tree:       2
              / \
             1   3

  Choose root = 3:
    left = [1,2]      right = []
    left shapes: 2 trees   right shapes: [null]
    Trees:     3          3
              /          /
             1          2
              \        /
               2      1

  Total: 2 + 1 + 2 = 5 = Catalan(3)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Generating all structurally unique BSTs for values 1 through N uses divide and conquer driven by the BST ordering invariant. For each value chosen as root, everything smaller goes left and everything larger goes right. You recursively generate every possible left shape and right shape, then pair each combination under the root to form complete trees.

The empty-range sentinel is the detail that makes the recursion correct. When a range is empty, returning a list with one null (not an empty list) ensures the pairing loop executes once and correctly produces trees where the root has only one child. Without this, those trees are silently lost.

The count of unique BST shapes is the Catalan number, which grows exponentially. Counting alone uses DP in O(n^2), but generation must construct all C(n)*n tree nodes, so it is practical only for small N.

At the National Bank of India, the analytics team benchmarks interest-tier lookup trees. Tiers 1 through N can be arranged in many valid BST shapes, and each shape gives different worst-case and average lookup depths. Generating all shapes for small tier counts lets the team pick the one with the best average depth, and the Catalan count tells them how many shapes to expect.

Remember one sentence: make each value the root, recurse for left and right shapes, pair them, and return [null] for empty ranges so one-child trees are not lost.
